title: Pip Sat
checkpoint: Reception Autumn 1, week 3 — after s, a, t, p, i, n, m, d (Learning — Phase 2)
note_for_grown_ups: Wren's very first book. It only uses the sounds taught so far (s, a, t, p and i), so the sentences are deliberately tiny — that's normal this early. Even Pip's name can be sounded out: p-i-p.

pages.illustration: Pip the sand-brown tufted sparrow sitting alone on a bare patch of earth, filling most of the page. Nothing else in shot. The whole meaning of this five-word book is carried by the pictures, so make him big, warm and immediately likeable.
Pull back to show an old brass garden tap on a low brick wall, Pip perched on the spout. A single drip hanging off the end. Plenty of clean space so the four words have room.
Close on the tap, three drips caught at different heights below it, Pip tapping the metal with his beak. Show the sound as ripples in a puddle underneath rather than as letters.
Pip patting the puddle with one foot, water rings spreading. His expression is delighted and slightly naughty. Bright splash of water against the muted brick.
Wide closing view: Pip sitting back in the sunny puddle he has made, thoroughly wet and thoroughly pleased, wet footprints leading away across the paving.
